tldr: The note proves that retaining trial labels can strictly improve minimax inference when unequal recruitment leaves finite rare-subgroup information about a transported treatment contrast. Its Gaussian--Poisson formulation keeps the dense variance \(4/5\), the full target-compatible contrast polygon, independently unknown intensities, and separately observed subgroup totals. It gives all-procedure original-data limits and data-only attainment for squared risk and uniformly honest connected intervals, certified finite programs for labeled and count-preserving pooled values, and convergent brackets for both information prices. Equal common path intensities give zero price, while a computable open unequal-intensity region has strictly positive prices for both squared risk and connected-interval length.
gap: The internal four-cycle manuscript characterizes a mixed precision frontier, exact common-intensity pooling, and edge-deletion losses. Its explicit honest scope excludes a comparison with the best robust pooled rule. A nonancillary edge label or excess risk of one balanced rule does not establish such a minimax gap. Published regular transport, Gaussian network resistance, signed transformations, and generic confidence games are supporting ancestors.
fill: The label-retention theorem matches the labeled and count-preserving pooled all-procedure original-data values on the identical causal class. A full-polygon labeled upper rule is paired with explicit legal pooled-data perturbations, a certified Hellinger lower bound, and a quantitative affinity limit over a broad compact family of unequal-intensity specifications. These yield a computable positive price on an open region, retaining every feasible learned macrocontrast. Connected-interval information loss is posed separately through the coverage-constrained game handle.
